rows.text: A short blade with a close-fitting grip. The point has been kept sharp.
A compact sword with a straight edge and enough grip to keep the hand behind the guard.
A long, straight blade balanced above a plain crossguard.
A broad sword with a long grip and a guard that spreads well clear of the blade.
A large blade with room for both hands on the hilt. Its reach begins well beyond the grip.
A short haft carries a wedge-shaped head. The back of the blade is thick enough to take a knock.
A broad axe head sits on a reinforced haft. The cutting edge curves away from the socket.
A stout club, heavier at the striking end and smoothed where a hand holds it.
A heavy head on a short haft. Its raised faces concentrate the weight of a blow.
A dense striking head is fixed across a long handle. The face is narrower than the mass behind it.
A narrow point extends from a long shaft. The join is bound close beneath the head.
Panels of thick leather are joined where the body needs to bend. The fastening straps show repeated use.
Small metal rings overlap in a flexible mesh. Their weight gathers wherever the garment folds.
Shaped plates overlap at the joints, with straps holding each section against the body.
A small shield with a raised centre and a grip behind it.
A compact iron shield. Its turned rim leaves a shallow bowl behind the face.
A worked iron shell with an opening for the face. The rim has been turned away from the skin.
Supple leather boots with thicker soles and reinforced seams around the toes.
Iron strengthens the soles of these boots. Scuffs mark the places that meet the ground first.
Close-fitting gloves with extra leather across the palms.
A fitted leather cap, stitched in curved panels to follow the head.
A broad piece of cloth with a fastening at the neck. Its hem carries the wear of travel.
Fine stitching follows the edges of this cloak. The repeated pattern continues around the fastening.
A woody trunk rises from a spread of roots. Branches fill the space above it.
Low branches and leaves form a close tangle near the ground.
Interwoven stems have thickened into a wall. More growth knots around the older strands.
Jointed stems stand close together, with narrow leaves folded along their sides.
Boards enclose a cargo space. Its corners bear the marks of lifting and stacking.
A hinged lid closes over a deep storage box. The frame is reinforced at the corners.
Coarse cloth is gathered at the mouth. The folds conceal whatever has been packed inside.
A close weave rises to a stiff rim, making a light container for things that need carrying.
The centre of the wood is hollow. The opening leaves room to store small things inside.
A seat and back are joined above a set of legs. The places hands rest are worn smooth.
Straw fills the sleeping place. The top has been pressed flat and gathered up again.
Stones mark a place for a fire. Ash has collected between them.
Hands and hauled ropes have polished the rim. The water lies below.
A counter gives someone a place to set out goods. Trading belongs to whoever tends it.
Wild berries cluster among the leaves. The fruit can be gathered.
Wax cells crowd the inside. Some hold honey.
